units.source: Sharing
units.context: Sharing

units.source: Trilium allows you to share selected notes as __TRILIUM_PH_0__publicly accessible__TRILIUM_PH_1__ read-only documents. This feature is particularly useful for publishing content directly from your Trilium notes, making it accessible to others online.
units.context: Sharing

units.source: Features, interaction and limitations__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Searching by note title.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Light and dark mode, following the visitor's system setting by default, also while the page is open. The visitor can pick __TRILIUM_PH_0__Light__TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__Dark__TRILIUM_PH_3__ or __TRILIUM_PH_4__System__TRILIUM_PH_5__ with the buttons at the top of the navigation pane; the choice is remembered by the browser.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: A layout centered on wide screens, with the navigation tree and the table of contents at either side of the content, and a mobile-friendly layout on narrow ones. There, the navigation tree slides in from the menu button in the header, and lists the headings of the current page below its entry (at the top of the pane, for a page the tree does not show).
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Collapsible tree with the same note icons as the application. It keeps the sections the visitor expanded and its scroll position while they move between the pages of the site, and shows the current note.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Customizable logo.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Quick navigation buttons (previous and next note).
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Notes that hide their children from the tree with __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (such as a __TRILIUM_PH_1__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_2__) show a badge counting them in place of listing them. The page of one of those children shows only that child below its parent, and the previous and next buttons skip them.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: The subpages of a text or code note shown below its content as cards, as in the application. Each card shows the icon of the subpage and the start of its text (or its __TRILIUM_PH_0__), or, for a subpage without text, links to its own first subpages. The cards can be hidden with __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Displaying the date of the last update of the note, written out in the application's language.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Marking the page with the application's language and its text direction, and the content of the note with its own __TRILIUM_PH_0__content language__TRILIUM_PH_1__, for screen readers and right-to-left text.
units.context: Sharing > Features, interaction and limitations

units.source: Prerequisites__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Prerequisites

units.source: To use the sharing feature, you must have a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Server Installation__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of Trilium. This is necessary because the notes will be hosted from the server.
units.context: Sharing > Prerequisites

units.source: Sharing a note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Sharing a note

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Enable Sharing__TRILIUM_PH_1__: To share a note, toggle the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ switch within the note's interface. Once sharing is enabled, an URL will appear, which you can click to access the shared note.
units.context: Sharing > Sharing a note

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Access the Shared Note__TRILIUM_PH_1__: The link provided will open the note in your browser. If your server is not configured with a public IP, the URL will refer to __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Sharing > Sharing a note

units.source: Sharing a note subtree__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Sharing a note subtree

units.source: When you share a note, you actually share the entire subtree of notes beneath it. If the note has child notes, they will also be included in the shared content. For example, sharing the "Formatting" subtree will display a page with basic navigation for exploring all the notes within that subtree.
units.context: Sharing > Sharing a note subtree

units.source: Viewing and managing shared notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Viewing and managing shared notes

units.source: You can view a list of all shared notes by clicking on __TRILIUM_PH_0__Advanced__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Shared notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4__Global menu__TRILIUM_PH_5__. This allows you to manage and navigate through all the notes you have made public.
units.context: Sharing > Viewing and managing shared notes

units.source: Security considerations__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Security considerations

units.source: Shared notes are published on the open internet and can be accessed by anyone with the URL unless the notes are password-protected.
units.context: Sharing > Security considerations

units.source: The URL's randomness does not provide security, so it is crucial not to share sensitive information through this feature.
units.context: Sharing > Security considerations

units.source: Trilium takes precautions to protect your publicly shared instance from leaking information for non-shared notes, including opening a separate read-only connection to the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Database__TRILIUM_PH_1__. Depending on your threat model, it might make more sense to use __TRILIUM_PH_2__Exporting static HTML for web publishing__TRILIUM_PH_3__ and use battle-tested web servers such as Nginx or Apache to serve static content.
units.context: Sharing > Security considerations

units.source: Password protection__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Security considerations > Password protection

units.source: To protect shared notes with a username and password, you can use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute. Add this label to the note with the format __TRILIUM_PH_1__. To protect an entire subtree, make sure the label is __TRILIUM_PH_2__inheritable__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Sharing > Security considerations > Password protection

If you want this style to apply to the entire subtree, make the label inheritable. You can hide the CSS code note from the tree navigation by adding the __TRILIUM_PH_5__ label.
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Customizing the appearance of shared notes

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Omitting Default CSS__TRILIUM_PH_1__: For extensive styling changes, use the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ label to avoid conflicts with Trilium's __TRILIUM_PH_3__default stylesheet__TRILIUM_PH_4__.

units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Adding JavaScript

units.source: You can inject custom JavaScript into the shared note using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation. This allows you to access note attributes or traverse the note tree using the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ API, which retrieves note data based on its ID.
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Adding JavaScript

units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Adding custom HTML

units.source: Creating human-readable URL aliases__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Creating human-readable URL aliases

units.source: Shared notes typically have URLs like __TRILIUM_PH_0__, where the last part is the note's ID. You can make these URLs more user-friendly by adding the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ label to individual notes (e.g., __TRILIUM_PH_2__). This will change the URL to __TRILIUM_PH_3__. The URL with the note's ID keeps working and redirects to the alias.

units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Setting a custom favicon

units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Setting a custom favicon

units.source: Sharing a note as the root__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Sharing a note as the root

units.source: You can designate a specific note or folder as the root of your shared content by adding the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. This note will be linked when visiting __TRILIUM_PH_1__, making it easier to use Trilium as a fully-fledged website.
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Sharing a note as the root

units.source: Consider combining this with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label, which will display a list of all shared notes.
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Sharing a note as the root

units.source: Displaying an index of shared notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Displaying an index of shared notes

units.source: When accessing a share, the sub-notes will be displayed in a tree on the left. But since multiple note trees can be shared, it might be useful to display a list of all the different share trees.
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Displaying an index of shared notes

units.source: To do so, create a shared text note and apply the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. When viewed, the list of shared roots will be displayed at the bottom of the note.
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Displaying an index of shared notes

units.source: Linking to an external website__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Linking to an external website

units.source: Sometimes it's useful to include a link to an external website alongside your shared notes — for example in the shared navigation or in an index. To do so, add the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label to a note, with the target URL as its value (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_1__).
units.context: Sharing > Advanced sharing options > Linking to an external website
